- **ep**: Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche — previously Donald Trump's personal criminal defence attorney — personally interviewed Maxwell over two days at the US Attorney's office in Tallahassee in late July 2025. DOJ granted her limited immunity to discuss her case and released a transcript. Senators Whitehouse and Durbin wrote that it is highly unusual, if not unprecedented, for the second-ranking official at the Justice Department to conduct such an interview rather than a line prosecutor familiar with the case. The interview followed the July memo in which DOJ and the FBI announced no further Epstein documents would be released.
- **ep**: No reason was given at the time. Blanche subsequently said on Meet the Press that the decision was made by the Bureau of Prisons and was justified because Maxwell had received numerous threats against her life, though he did not elaborate on them; he added that every BOP decision lands on his desk to the extent it needs to. At his 2026 Senate Judiciary confirmation hearing as acting Attorney General he repeated the safety rationale, and Senator Cory Booker called it an absurdity. Senator Whitehouse formally demanded documents from the BOP director, writing that she was transferred without explanation and in possible violation of standard Bureau policy.
- **ep**: In March 2026 the House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Bondi over the Department's handling of the files, with five Republicans joining Democrats in the vote. In April 2026 Trump fired her. On May 29, 2026 she gave a closed-door transcribed interview to House Oversight, telling the panel that redaction errors were made, that she had been assured by the reviewing team that only non-responsive, privileged or duplicative material was withheld, and that to the best of her knowledge the Department produced everything required. She refused to discuss the President's involvement in the handling of the files. Todd Blanche, her deputy, became acting Attorney General.

- **billclinton**: Journalist Katie Phang sued over the withholding. U.S. District Judge Emmet Sullivan ruled the administration 'likely violated' the Act — a judicial finding, this rubric's strongest evidentiary tier. Acting AG Todd Blanche himself conceded the violation. As of an Aug. 13, 2026 hearing, Sullivan was still pressing DOJ attorneys on compliance, noting he'd held government lawyers in contempt before in his career, though no contempt finding has been issued in this matter as of that date.
- **doj**: Trump fired Bondi on April 2, 2026. His public statement gave no reason. Acting AG Todd Blanche publicly denied Epstein was the cause; multiple outlets contemporaneously reported it was the primary cause. [cite:complexinsights_epstein_files] Bondi's own subsequent testimony blamed Blanche — characterizing him as the official 'in charge of the entire release' — her own former deputy, whom Trump had just promoted to replace her.

- **ep_OPERATIONS_v1.md**: *What happened (documented):* - Maxwell was convicted in December 2021 on five counts, including **sex trafficking of a minor**, and sentenced to 20 years. She was held at **FCI Tallahassee, a low-security prison**. - In late July 2025 she sat for about nine hours of interviews over two days with **Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche**, in Tallahassee. Her lawyer said they discussed "about 100 names". - On **1 August 2025**, days later, the Bureau of Prisons moved her to **FPC Bryan, Texas, a minimum-security camp**. The BOP gave no reason.
